chapter: The Dallas nightclub and Jesse Stone's band
title: Jesse Stone auditions the Dallas musicians
summary: Jesse Stone, hired as musical director, gives each local musician a reading test at Arthur Alexander's house.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Reading music versus faking and playing by ear

blocks.x: So we went home, my brother and I, and when we got there we were met by a man by the name of Jesse Stone. Somehow, T. H. Smith had heard of Jesse Stone's musical abilities. I don't know who recommended him, and he was a giant, to come and be the musical director, and write all of the music for the show, and they had hired a show out of Chicago. In other words, Milt, you might remember, Flute and Joiner? That's (inaudible). And the floor show, and all. They had hired out of Chicago.

And it was really big time, but now what had happened, I'm back with all of my old friends from the Blue Moon chasers, and we being the best jazz musicians in town, naturally all of these guys were informed what was going on, and was told to come by. Now Jesse Stone was a very methodical man.
Jesse Stone had gone to the University of Nebraska, and was one of the first black athletes on the track team there. Also, he majored in music.

Was a great arranger even then, so we went over -- he set up shop in one of my friend's home, who had a good piano, and everything, named Arthur Alexander, who I mentioned before, that was with us. He played alto and clarinet. And he would call us there and one by one he would have us to come into the room and he would throw a piece of music up and he would play the accompaniment on the piano, and he'd say, 'play this.' He was giving us an aptitude test, in other words. But not like you might do it with kids who haven't played an instrument, but with musicians, to see if they were capable of playing his music for this show.
